subject: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@vectra.ai>, Amit Desai <amit@vectra.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks

Hi Sana / Amit,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — quick follow-up with the data we discussed. We pulled a short ROI deck and a CSV of token usage by route for April–May to make the renewal conversation concrete. Two items we want to align on before the renewal call next week:

1) Observed SLA gaps: your p99 has a handful of spikes during peak batch jobs; our ops team sees these correlate with long prefix-queries that could be mitigated by a small cache bump.
2) Commit sizing: your current run-rate plus planned feature rollout suggests a realistic 30% headroom to avoid overages in Q3.

Attachments: 20260514-vectra-usage-ROI-deck.pdf (summary slides), vectra_kpi_export_May.csv (per-route tokens)

Ask: Can you confirm whether procurement needs a 60-day notice for any term/PO changes? Also, would Friday 10am PT work for a 30-min alignment?

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Sana Rao <sana@vectra.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@vectra.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks

Jonas — thanks for the deck, skimmed the CSV. A couple quick notes:

- Procurement: 30 days is the internal target but legal sometimes needs extra time for amendments. 60 days would be safe if there are contract language changes.
- SLA: the spikes you noted impacted a live workflow last week; our eng lead (Amit) will join the call to walk through the trace.
- On commit: we are open to a larger committed tier if you can guarantee some burst credits for the first month while we migrate traffic. Can you quantify what "small cache bump" means?

Friday 10am PT works. Please include a proposed commit tier and a one-page summary of rollback/fallback in case perf regressions occur.

— Sana
Head of Platform, Vectra.ai

Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks

> Friday 10am PT works. Please include a proposed commit tier and a one-page summary of rollback/fallback in case perf regressions occur.

Adding detail on the spike: it coincided with a nightly batch of long-context document summarization (avg seq len ~6k). We saw latency p95~1.2s and p99 moments hitting ~3.8s; duration was about 4–6 minutes. If you have cached prefix windows or a way to prioritize holding KV cache across that job, it would help.

I'll be on the call and can share logs.
— Amit
Senior Engineering Manager, Vectra.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@vectra.ai>, Amit Desai <amit@vectra.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks

Hi team — quick internal sync then the proposed materials for the Friday call (attached). Summary of what we can offer:

- Technical mitigation: Ops can apply a targeted KV cache window increase for the long-context job and pin the job to a lower-latency routing pool during the nightly window. Expect p99 improvement from ~3.8s -> ~1.1–1.6s in early testing.
- Commercial: For a 12-month committed tier at 1.3x current run-rate we can offer: 10% below list unit price, plus 1 month of 50k token burst credits for migration.
- Rollback/fallback: We will provide an automatic fallback to the previous model variant and route traffic to a reserve pool should latency breach the agreed SLO. One-page summary attached.

Attachments: 20260517-vectra-rollforward-summary.pdf (1-page fallback), 20260514-vectra-usage-ROI-deck.pdf (updated)

As requested, Friday 10am PT is confirmed — calendar invite sent. Any objections to the 1.3x commit sizing? If you prefer we can size a staged ramp (1.1x for Q3 then 1.5x starting Q4) instead.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Sana Rao <sana@vectra.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@vectra.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage + SLA gap review — renewal rollforward asks

Jonas / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the concrete options. We reviewed internally:

- Technical: Amit confirmed the mitigation plan looks sensible; we'll test in staging this week.
- Commercial: Procurement is leaning toward the staged ramp you proposed (1.1x Q3, 1.5x Q4) with the burst credits applied immediately. Legal will need the one-page rollback section to include explicit SLO thresholds.
- Timeline: We should be able to confirm the final PO by June 15 if Redwood can provide the updated addendum language and the HubSpot deal note with the staged commit milestones.

Please send the one-line SLO thresholds and a draft amendment (redline preferred) and we'll route to legal. Call notes tomorrow will include timelines.

Thanks — Sana
